findings.evidence: Table 5-2, row 'Total tokens per dollar (serial single-stream floor, no overlap; 20 ms/token basis)': "~242,000 tokens per dollar (~199,000 at the canonical 25 ms/token)" with derivation "9,500/7.08 ≈ 1,342 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20; 7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode at the illustrative 20 ms/token rate; at the canonical 25 ms/token, 9,500/8.58 ≈ 1,107 tok/s ≈ 199,000 tokens/$"
findings.issue: The row is labeled [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] and its derivation is correct. However, the table mixes two different operating points in a single row — the 20 ms/token illustrative basis (242,000) and the canonical 25 ms/token basis (199,000) — and the row label says '20 ms/token basis' while the parenthetical adds a second basis. The §5.3(b) text (p. 108) correctly separates these as 'three figures are stated on different bases and are not one series', but the table row itself presents them as one metric with a parenthetical. A reader scanning the table could lift ~242,000 without noticing the canonical-basis counterpart is ~199,000. This is a clarity/labeling risk, not an arithmetic defect.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the row into two rows or move the ~199,000 figure to a separate footnote line, so each row carries exactly one basis and one provenance tag.

findings.evidence: "single‑core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), beyond that typical sustained range — conditional on measured single-core throughput."
findings.issue: The sentence is grammatically broken: 'fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s ... beyond that typical sustained range' reads as if 92.8 is beyond the range, but the intended meaning is that the required 92.8 GFLOP/s is beyond the 30–60 GFLOP/s typical sustained range, so single-core encoding does NOT fit. The clause 'beyond that typical sustained range' has no clear antecedent and the sentence lacks a main verb connecting the two halves. This is a prose clarity defect (ASD-STE100) that could mislead a reader into thinking single-core encoding fits.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as: 'single-core encoding would require ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), which is beyond the typical 30–60 GFLOP/s sustained range — so single-core encoding does not fit the ~120 ms retrieval budget, conditional on measured single-core throughput.'
